selection.symbolic_inputs: three typed event-history lanes with arbitrary value kinds, values, and fixed-point ownership
selection.exhaustive_test_infeasible_because: the product of typed values, ownership masks, and invalid-input positions is not practically enumerable
selection.counterexample_means: event-history advancement can lose type fidelity or partially mutate pre values on rejection

assumptions: typed_value generates only lattice-valid values (Real from i16/4.0, Integer whole f64, Boolean 0/1, Enumeration >= 1), so the kernel's type-validity clauses are exercised only through the single injected invalid position
the invalid injection is a NaN placed in the last lane's current value, so rejection is proven for that representative invalid typed input rather than every invalid encoding
unwind bound 16 covers the three lanes at the harness's fixed iteration shape; a wider lane count or a different iteration shape is outside the proof
advance_event_iteration_lanes is the production kernel; callers that bypass it or mutate EventIterationLane fields directly are outside the proof
Kani models f64 bit patterns exactly, so to_bits comparisons stand in for unchanged-value equality including NaN payloads

bound.domain: three production event-history lanes with arbitrary value kinds, typed values, fixed-point ownership, and invalid-input injection
